emittedReviewed.rationale: Score 73, rank 42, 5/36 qualifying periods. Williamsburg Bridge shuttle: essentially a single bridge segment, so top-decile speed is structural and the persistence is thin. Reviewer-visible as a peer-group degenerate case, not a learning candidate.

Score 91, rank 12, 36/36 qualifying periods. A Bronx local in the densest borough family sustaining top-decile speed across all 36 periods is the strongest learning candidate in the batch: the fleet-wide peer group biases toward express routes, and BX29 outperforms despite that bias.

Score 70, rank 48, only 2/36 qualifying periods. Express service-class artifact (fleet-wide peer group) compounded by fragile persistence at the minimum qualifying-period count: nothing here grades as a learnable practice.

Score 79, rank 32, 7/36 qualifying periods. M35 serves Randall's Island over the RFK bridge: a short, structurally uncongested route. The speed is real but the route is sui generis and the persistence thin; keep visible to reviewers as a peer-group counterexample, no internal study action.

Score 71, rank 47, only 2/36 qualifying periods — at the minimum persistence gate. Two qualifying months out of three years is indistinguishable from noise or a transient data artifact; not a real persistent outperformer.

Score 100, rank 1, 36/36 qualifying periods against the 348-route fleet peer group. Q35 is a local route in dense Brooklyn/Queens territory, so its persistent top-decile average_speed_mph is not explained purely by service class. Worth internal study of stop spacing and the Marine Parkway corridor; counter-evidence caveat (covariates/residuals before attribution) stands.

Score 94, rank 8, 36/36 qualifying periods. Local Queens/Bronx route with persistent outperformance not attributable to express service class. The long Whitestone Bridge segment inflates speed, so the learning question is corridor mix — still a genuine internal-study candidate.

Score 82, rank 24, 9/36 qualifying periods. Express commuter route compared against the fleet-wide 'NYC bus routes with speed-history support' peer group: highway running and limited-stop patterns make top-decile average_speed_mph structural, not deviant. A false deviant for learning purposes — the peer group fails to condition on service class. Only 9/36 qualifying periods adds fragility on top of the class artifact.
